title: Rollops — Rollout operations for the agentic web
description: Lean, infrastructure-agnostic rollout orchestration where agents and humans are peer operators. The engine is a Go library at the center; CLI, daemon, MCP, and UI are thin clients over it. Built on the Klarlatz stack (statekit, axi-go, fortify, decision-kit, bolt, mcp-go, mnemos). No Kubernetes dependency in core; runs on a bare VPS. v1 risk and rollback are observability-free. Source of desired state is Git; the Store holds runtime state only. This spec covers the P0 OSS core and the P2 ecosystem/scale layer.

constraints.description: Core has no Kubernetes dependency. K8s is one target plugin, never an assumption.
v1 risk scoring and auto-rollback use no metrics. Metric-based analysis is Phase 2 (Obvia seam); do not bake it in.
Git is the only source of desired state. The Store holds runtime state only; losing it must never corrupt what should be deployed.
Conditional logic uses embedded CEL. No bespoke DSL. relicta's governance DSL stays separate.
Secrets are never stored locally. Vault via SecretProvider; redact secret material at the audit/log/diff/MCP boundary.
gRPC, REST, and MCP require mTLS or signed tokens. RBAC on operations. The MCP agent surface is privileged.
Agent limits are hard, not advisory — non-bypassable policy floor, kill-switch, full attribution, fortify rate-limit.
Single Go binary + SQLite is the common case. First-party targets compiled in. Every feature justifies its weight.
Reuse statekit, axi-go, fortify, decision-kit, bolt, mcp-go, mnemos rather than reinventing.
